questions.answer: The nature was a big reason that I picked Oslo, and the quietness of the city itself.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.answer: The Sogn student housing is filled with other exchange students, so you always have someone to connect with

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
SIO did not answer my emails, and didn't fix my freezer in all of the time I was there.

I also got a room that was right beside some very loud workers, that started yelling at 6 in the morning every day, even after I send an email to SIO, and put a note to them

questions.answer: Very easy, but it's a long time ago, so I don't remember it that well

questions.answer: You could talk with the office for help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *

questions.answer: Remember to ask for help if you need it

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'm studying Musicology at KU, and the courses I took in Oslo, was not only for music students, so the level of theory was not that high, but still interesting. Wish they would had said that on the website before I came

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more reading and sitting down, with no physical training like playing music

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as a danish person

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think it was much easier for me as I understand Norwegian, but on thing that helped me socialize was joining the student pubs, like U1 and Uglebo

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Very close to the danish way, so I didn't find it challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The calmness of the everyday life

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to join the student pubs

Remeber to take a break sometimes and relax in your room

The campus is a great place to sit and relax/study

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world, and getting new ways of looking at nationalities I didn't have beforehand

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Some of the other cultures were very loud after quiet hours, which was a little hard to get use to.

I had a lot of nights where I didn't sleep, because of culture difference in volume of speaking, and just the time of day people are awake.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
